native_result.query: In the PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices, during the Younger Bronze Age (1100-500 BCE), how does the principal component value of PC1 in the beginning of the period at 1100 BCE differ from the subsequent time horizons between 1000 to 500 BCE?
native_result.HypoA: The beginning of the Younger Bronze Age (1100 BCE) is associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1), while the majority of time horizons (1000-500 BCE) are characterized by positive values on PC1. This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: During the Younger Bronze Age (1100-500 BCE), the hundred-year-slice PCA on the forms of capital has PC1 strongly positive and at its highest at 1100 BCE (PC1 ~ +4.45) and markedly higher than at all later horizons (1000 BCE ~ +2.17, 900 ~ +1.65, 800 ~ +1.91, 700 ~ +1.25, 600 ~ +0.83, 500 ~ +0.82; mean ~ +1.44), i.e., PC1 at 1100 BCE is ~ +3.0 higher than the average of the 1000-500 BCE slices and declines across the period. On the loadings-defined axis (positive Copper&Gold, Pottery decoration, Depot, Hatchets&Swords, Daggers, Monument Size, House Size, Monument Count), 1100 BCE is a peak of accumulated social/symbolic/economic capital that then drops substantially and stays low through 1000-500 BCE.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded capital.csv and parsed German comma-decimal Z-values; verified 39 hundred-year slices (BCE 4300->500, step 100), 0 NAs, YBA window = 7 slices (1100,1000,900,800,700,600,500 BCE). Cross-checked identical raw values vs time_series_data.csv at the 100-yr marks (444/444). 2) Single shared PCA on the 12 Z columns (all 39 slices), centered (verified corr 1.0000 vs uncentered => z-scores already standardized); computed PC1 scores, loadings, evr via numpy SVD. 3) Compared PC1 at 1100 BCE (baseline anchor, first YBA slice) vs each later slice 1000-500 BCE and vs their mean; reported signed differences with loadings to fix axis orientation. 4) Documented sensitivity: PCA refit on the 7-slice YBA subset (same substantive axis, flipped sign). 5) Wrote results to analysis/results_YBA_PC1.json. No paper figure numerics assumed; only computed values used.
